boxes.text: Using @mpemode 1, the mc.noteallocator~ voice is equal to the MPE voice as output by the mpeparse object. This means the MPE source (keyboard, MIDI file etc.) controls voice allocation.

mc.noteallocator~ associates a voice number with a MIDI event. The voice number can be a channel index for MC objects or poly~ voices. mc.noteallocator~ keeps track of busy voices. If there is a multichannel signal connected to mc.noteallocator~, the busy state is based on a non-zero level of the audio input on each channel. If no signal is connected, mc.noteallocator~ uses MIDI note-ons and note-offs to determine the busy state. In this case, a voice is defined to be busy from the time it is allocated with a note-on until a corresponding note-off is received.
the voice number is output just before each MIDI event

Using the @name attribute, you can assign a name to mc.noteallocator~'s busy map, which makes it available in all patchers. (Without a name, the mc.noteallocator~ busy map works only in its patcher.) Objects that want to use a named busy map need to have their @busymapname set to the designated name.
when an audio signal is not connected to mc.noteallocator~ all voices start out busy by default until the first note-on is received
send note-offs to turn the busy map voice off
send note-ons to turn a  busy map voice on
you can use mc.sig~ 1 to monitor the busy map: it will output zero when a non-busy voice is not being used

Each instance of mc.noteallocator~ holds a busy map that optimizes MC wrapper objects. When these objects have their @usebusymap attribute set to 1, any non-busy voices are not computed. The busy map is controlled from either MIDI note messages or an incoming audio signal.
